title: Orientation
text:
Course Overview

Duration: ~12 Weeks
Format: 2-4 sessions per week (Tue-Fri, 7:00–8:30 PM IST)
Style: Lectures, demos and labs
Assessment: Quizzes, assignments, and final project/presentation
Credits: 3 + 1 (Credits added in ABC)

title: Orientation
text:
Why This Course?
LLMs have changed how we build intelligent applications.
This course aims to bridge the gap between:
Using LLMs via APIs -> Engineering LLM systems

title: Orientation
text:
Learning Outcomes

Understand LLM architectures
Understanfd GPU programming and optimization techniques
Optimize inference for cost and latency
Fine-tune models for specific domains and tasks
Build robust LLM-powered applications (RAG, agents, tool use)
Evaluate, debug, and improve model performance
Leverage open-source ecosystems for LLM engineering

title: Orientation
section: What This Course Will NOT Cover
text:
What This Course Will NOT Cover

Mathematical foundations
Pretraining LLMs from scratch
State of the art in research
Data engineering pipelines
Ethics and societal impacts

title: Orientation
text:
Course Roadmap (1/2)







Module
Topic




1
LLM Foundations - Transformers, GPT-2, Modern Architectures, MoE, OSS Models


2
GPUs - Architecture and Programming, Multi-GPU Parallelism,


3
Inference - Sampling, KV Caching, Quantization, Speculative Decoding, Model Serving


4
RAG & Agents - RAG Fundamentals, ReAct, Tools, Protocols, Agents, Finetuning


5
Evaluation - Moderl Evaluations, Benchmarks, LLM-as-a-Judge

Topic

Edge Deployment - Edge architectures, Optimization and Deployment

title: Lesson 01 — Intro to LLMs
text:
What is a language model?
A function that, given a prefix of tokens, returns a probability distribution over the next token.

Speaker notes: anchor the discussion in the prediction objective before introducing transformers.

title: Lesson 01 — Intro to LLMs
text:
Why now?

Compute is cheap and parallel
The web gave us trillions of tokens
Attention scales better than recurrence

title: Lesson 01 — Intro to LLMs
text:
What we’ll build toward

A working mental model of how a transformer predicts the next token
Comfort reading inference-time code (sampling, KV cache, batching)
Practical fluency with the tradeoffs in fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. prompting
